tagline: Colorado's first scenic highway, down the Front Range from Estes Park.
intro: From Estes Park, where it meets Trail Ridge Road, the Peak to Peak Highway runs south along the Front Range with the Continental Divide in view, through Allenspark, Ward and Nederland and down past Rollinsville to Black Hawk, 55 miles in all. Gravel roads branch off to high lakes, to the ghost towns of Hesse and Apex, and to the Moffat Tunnel's east portal.

The road was laid out in 1918, the first scenic highway in Colorado. Allenspark, near its north end, takes its name from Alonzo Allen, a miner who built a cabin there in 1864. A settler who came later said all Allen ever did for Allenspark was give it a name.

moments.title: Chapel on the Rock
moments.text: Monsignor Joseph Bosetti found the rock in 1916 and spent nearly twenty years raising money and struggling with the state highway department to keep it intact before the chapel was finished in 1936.

moments.title: Ward
moments.text: A gold camp at 9,450 feet, nearly deserted by the 1920s, revived by the highway, down to four year-round residents in the war, and repopulated by hippies in the 1960s.

moments.title: Nederland
moments.text: Dayton, then Browns Crossing, then Middle Boulder, until Dutch miners milling Caribou ore here called it Nederland, meaning low land, a name the town adopted in 1874.
